question.worked_solution:
If we let $u=\frac{x}{3},$ then

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{3}\,⟹\,\text{d}x=3\,\text{d}u.
$$

Calculating the limits for $u$ gives

| $x$ | $0$ | $\pi $ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $0$ | $\pi /3$ |

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sec}⁡(\frac{x}{3})\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{x}{3})\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /3}\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sec}⁡u\operatorname{tan}⁡u\cdot 3\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{3}{2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /3}\operatorname{sec}⁡u\operatorname{tan}⁡u\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{3}{2}\operatorname{sec}⁡u{|}_{0}^{\pi /3} \\  & =\frac{3}{2}(\operatorname{sec}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3})-\operatorname{sec}⁡(0)) \\  & =\frac{3}{2}(2-1) \\  & =\frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}
$$
